title: Cloud Architect Operator Bootcamp
purpose: A career-changer pathway toward strong cloud architecture, security, automation, platform engineering, and technical leadership. The aim is not certification recall: every level makes you design, build, secure, operate, recover, explain, and improve a system.
scope_note: This is a curriculum blueprint with 72 lab briefs and nine fully specified capstone-style example labs. Cloud spend and service availability vary by account, region, and date; use the safety gates below, verify current provider behavior, and never run a lab in a production account.

operating_contract.intro: Each lab begins with its scenario and constraints. Every learner submission includes:
items: Working terminal evidence: commands, scripts, config, and reproducible results—not console screenshots.
Deterministic tests: `make validate` (or documented equivalent) exits nonzero on a failed requirement and avoids depending on live cloud state unless the lab explicitly tests a disposable deployment.
A failure drill: inject the named fault in a disposable environment, capture symptoms, diagnosis, recovery, and residual risk.
One decision record (`docs/adr/0001-*.md`) or the specifically requested runbook/incident report. Include context, decision, alternatives, consequences, and evidence.
A cleanup command and a post-cleanup check. Cloud labs must have a time limit, budget/alert where available, region allowlist, resource inventory, and teardown proof.
A short `REPORT.md`: what worked, what did not, test output, cost-control evidence, and next improvement.
operating_contract.acceptance_gate: Clean checkout → documented setup → `make validate` passes → failure drill is reproducible → cleanup completes → no lab-owned resources remain → required evidence and ADR/runbook/report exist. Each lab's brief adds its own acceptance tests. If a test requires cloud credentials, it must also have a deterministic offline/unit mode.
operating_contract.safety: Use a dedicated sandbox account/project/subscription, least-privilege lab role, synthetic data, no public ingress unless explicitly required, no real secrets in Git, region allowlists, short TTLs, and teardown even after a failed apply. Budget alerts are not hard spending caps. Never assume a destroy command succeeded—query and verify.

pacing: Progress by evidence, not calendar. Complete a level's eight labs in any order, then its exemplar as the level gate. A learner may split cloud labs across sessions; each session starts with a preflight and ends with cleanup verification.

directory_note: Each `labs/NN-slug/` is independently runnable and contains `README.md`, `src/` or `app/`, `tests/`, `scripts/`, `docs/`, and—only where needed—`infra/`. Keep generated state, credentials, plans containing sensitive values, logs with identifiers, and `.env` files out of Git. Pin tool versions and provider versions; commit lock files where appropriate.
lab_readme_template:
# Lab NN — Title

## Scenario and constraints
Who needs what? State scale, availability, data sensitivity, budget/time limit,
regions, permissions, and what is explicitly out of scope.

## Learning objectives
- Observable objective 1
- Observable objective 2

## Prerequisites and safety
Tool versions, sandbox identity, allowed regions, expected spend class, TTL,
credential check, and stop/cleanup rule. Never paste credentials into logs.

## Starter repository
List every relevant starter file and its purpose.

## Tasks (terminal-first)
Numbered commands/tasks, expected outputs, and where learner judgment is required.

## Failure injection
Fault, safe injection command, expected symptom, diagnosis evidence, recovery,
and how to restore the baseline. State what must never be injected in production.

## Deliverables
Code/config, tests, ADR or runbook or incident report, REPORT.md, and evidence paths.

## Validation and acceptance
`make validate`; unit/format/lint/security/policy tests; cloud integration checks;
explicit expected results and failure exit behavior.

## Cost controls and cleanup
Preflight; budget/alert if available; region/TTL/tagging; exact destroy command;
post-destroy inventory query; evidence that no lab-owned resources remain.

## Scoring (0–4 each)
Correctness, security, resilience, operational quality, cost, automation,
communication. Explain what 0, 2, and 4 mean for this lab.
catalog_note: The common operating contract above applies to **every** lab below: scenario + constraints, terminal tasks, failure drill, ADR/runbook/report, cleanup/cost controls, grading, and acceptance gate. Every brief lists its own starter directory, deterministic validator idea, and additional acceptance evidence. For every lab, implement `make validate` as an offline deterministic check plus an explicitly named, optional sandbox integration target. Use test fixtures, local emulators, mocks, or static policy tests for repeatability; never make routine validation create cloud resources.
exemplar_note: Each exemplar is a model of the expected depth and can be copied into its indicated directory. Use local/unit validation by default; cloud deployment is an opt-in, sandbox-only integration exercise. Do not paste output containing account IDs or private endpoints into public evidence.

validation.intro: The catalog's per-lab validation column names the lab-specific check. Implement this common pipeline consistently:
validation.makefile:
.PHONY: validate test lint policy integration clean
validate: lint test policy
lint:
	# formatters, static checks, shellcheck/ruff/terraform fmt as applicable

test:
	# offline deterministic tests; no credentials or cloud writes

policy:
	# IaC, IAM, secret, container, and documentation safety checks

integration:
	# opt-in only; requires sandbox preflight, explicit confirmation, and TTL

clean:
	# remove local artifacts created by this lab only
validation.layers_and_rules: Validation layers: (1) formatting/type/syntax, (2) unit tests with fixed fixtures, (3) security/policy negative tests, (4) reproducibility from clean checkout, (5) optional sandbox integration with explicit identity/region/resource boundary, (6) post-cleanup inventory assertion. Use pinned tools, fixed timestamps where relevant, deterministic sorting, and clear nonzero exit codes. Never make a validator silently skip a failed security check. Tests should cover both compliant and deliberately noncompliant fixtures. Treat cloud integration checks as evidence, not a substitute for deterministic unit tests.

before_write: Confirm sandbox account/project/subscription and principal via provider CLI; compare against an explicit local allowlist. If any identity value is unexpected or absent, stop.
Set an approved region/location allowlist. Keep default validation plan-only and offline.

Review `terraform plan` and estimate resource classes, data transfer, storage retention, logs, and possible idle time. Pricing changes; use the provider's current pricing source for a real estimate and record date/assumptions.
Apply resource tags/labels: `owner`, `bootcamp`, `lab`, `created_at`, `expires_at`, `environment`. Do not put secrets or personal data in tags.

Set a short TTL and a budget notification where available. Alerts are not hard caps. Avoid managed services with minimum charges, NAT gateways, public IPs, high-volume logs, GPUs, and cross-region/cross-cloud transfer unless a lab explicitly justifies them.
Use least-privilege, temporary credentials, no root/admin identity, and a clean `git status`. Never put credentials in Terraform variables committed to Git or shell history.
cost_and_teardown.apply_operate: Capture plan, resource inventory, and start time. Use low-volume synthetic data, bounded test duration, and explicit resource names. Stop immediately if resources exceed the approved scope.
cost_and_teardown.teardown: Run the lab-specific cleanup or `terraform destroy` from the same workspace; empty versioned object stores only when they are lab-owned and the procedure is documented. Then independently query inventory by lab tag/name and region. Check orphaned snapshots, logs, addresses, disks, versions, IAM bindings, and non-default networking resources as relevant. Save sanitized teardown evidence. `cleanup_verified=true` only after no lab-owned billable resources remain. If deletion fails, mark blocked, escalate through the sandbox owner, and do not claim cleanup success.
cost_and_teardown.guard_scripts: `scripts/preflight.sh` validates explicit provider/profile/project/subscription, allowlisted region, required lab ID and expiry, and rejects production-like identities; `scripts/teardown-check.sh` compares pre/post inventory snapshots for remaining lab-owned resources. Keep provider-specific resource discovery explicit and reviewed—never assume one generic tag query finds every resource.

portfolio.intro: Publish a curated set, not raw account dumps:

artifacts.title: Architecture case study
artifacts.guidance: anonymized problem, requirements, diagram source/render, options considered, ADR, failure analysis, accepted risks, and revisit triggers.

artifacts.title: Working repository
artifacts.guidance: reproducible local setup, deterministic tests, pinned dependencies, CI, security checks, and clear cleanup path.

artifacts.title: Security evidence
artifacts.guidance: threat model, least-privilege authorization matrix, negative tests, sanitized detection example, and remediation record.

artifacts.title: Operations evidence
artifacts.guidance: SLI/SLO definition, alert/runbook pair, synthetic incident timeline, restore test, RTO/RPO assumptions, and post-incident actions.

artifacts.title: Platform artifact
artifacts.guidance: golden-path template, policy-as-code fixtures, exception expiry workflow, developer documentation, and versioning plan.

artifacts.title: Multi-cloud judgment
artifacts.guidance: dated, sourced capability matrix that distinguishes true equivalence from superficially similar service names; explain provider-specific choices and exit costs.

artifacts.title: Leadership samples
artifacts.guidance: one-page executive brief, design review decision log, mentoring plan, and crisis tabletop with facts separated from hypotheses.

artifacts.title: Evidence index
artifacts.guidance: link each claim to a test, command transcript, ADR, or report. Sanitize account IDs, internal hostnames, personal data, credentials, and non-public incident details. Never claim a live production deployment or measured outcome unless the artifact proves it.

story_questions: What did you choose and reject?
How did you test security and failure behavior?
What did it cost to operate?
How do you know cleanup/recovery worked?
What evidence would make you change the decision?
